quote: In this sense the Church's Tradition has often read the most beautiful texts on wisdom in relation to Mary.

verifier.reason: §721 names no OT figure fulfilled in Mary. It reports that Tradition has 'read the most beautiful texts on wisdom in relation to Mary', which is a liturgical use of texts, and 'Seat of Wisdom' makes her the dwelling of Wisdom (Christ, 1 Cor 1:24), not Wisdom's antitype. At most this is a TEACHES row; a link, if wanted, would be Wisdom's dwelling place (Sir 24:8-12) → Mary, synthesized.

quotes.quote: Among these liturgical signs from the Old Covenant are circumcision, anointing and consecration of kings and priests, laying on of hands, sacrifices, and above all the Passover. The Church sees in these signs a prefiguring of the sacraments of the New Covenant.
The imposition of hands is rightly recognized by the Catholic tradition as the origin of the sacrament of Confirmation, which in a certain way perpetuates the grace of Pentecost in the Church.

verifier.reason: §1288 traces Confirmation's imposition of hands to the apostles and to Pentecost, not to any Old Testament gesture, and §1150 links the OT gesture only to the sacraments in general, so the Confirmation-specific pairing is not in the text. If a specific sacrament is wanted, §1538 (the laying on of hands as 'the visible sign of this ordination') with §1541 would support a tighter Holy Orders synthesis.

quote: The personal charism of some witnesses to God's love for men has been handed on, like "the spirit" of Elijah to Elisha and John the Baptist, so that their followers may have a share in this spirit.

verifier.reason: §2684 cites 'the spirit' of Elijah handed on 'to Elisha and John the Baptist' only as an analogy for how a founder's charism passes to his followers. Elisha's place in the same list shows the point is inheritance of a charism, not figure and fulfilment; if the Elijah-to-John link is wanted, §§717-720 is better ground.

quote: In many and various ways God spoke of old to our fathers by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son.

verifier.reason: §65 is about the completeness of revelation in the Son; the prophets appear only inside the Heb 1:1 quotation as earlier speakers of God's word 'in parts'. That is prophetic speech contrasted with the one Word, not the prophets as figures of Christ, so a TEACHES edge to `the-prophets` overreaches.
